title: Wasm source-kernel resource ownership closure
objective: Generate same-instance ownership-domain bridges for production source-transparent Wasm kernels that borrow or return declared FFI resources, prove generation-tagged lifecycle and real Wasm execution, and report the exact residual unsupported production surface

handoff.summary: Source-transparent Wasm bridges now borrow generation-tagged owned resources and adopt newly returned resources only through declaration-identified hooks linked into the same Wasm instance. The portable loader uses a trusted wrap/unwrap bridge, closes an adopted result when host wrapping is unavailable or fails, and never treats a handle as a foreign pointer. This closes all 18 production ownership-domain adapter classifications: 211 functions are bridgeable and the exact residual is seven extension-polynomial functions whose fq_context, fq_element, and fq_polynomial resources are not yet declared for Wasm. A real pinned FLINT reactor differential proves returned FmpqMatrix adoption, subsequent entry/count borrowing, memory growth, wrong and stale handle rejection, adoption-failure cleanup, idempotent host close, and zero final live resources.
risks: The shared tools/ffi generator must emit the declared borrow/adopt hooks and trusted backend wrap/unwrap bridge before these resource functions may be linked in the production artifact; linking without it fails closed.

The checked-in production-kernel coverage and capability reports still record 193 compiled and 25 unsupported functions because this lane may not claim shared generated release registries; integration must regenerate them to 211 and 7.
The seven fq extension functions remain intentionally unsupported until their three resource families receive reviewed Wasm declarations and real lifecycle tests.
next_steps: In tools/ffi/wasm-adapters.cjs, emit sagejs_wasm_resource_borrow_ID(handle, ABI_TYPE **value) and sagejs_wasm_resource_adopt_ID(ABI_TYPE value, uint64_t *handle) beside each owned resource table. Borrow must use the existing generation lookup. Adopt must reserve a slot, memcpy the ABI value as a move, mark it live, increment the live count, and publish the generation-tagged handle; failure leaves the caller-owned value untouched.

Have generated JavaScript expose a trusted ownership bridge bound to its backend brand and Wasm instance: unwrap validates the WeakMap brand, declaration identity, open state, and instance before returning a handle; wrap calls makeResource with the same brand/finalizer. Pass that bridge as instantiateWasmKernelPacks({resources}).

Link the generated FLINT resource adapter C and source-kernel bridge C into the same kernel-flint Wasm instance, pass its closure identity/sources/exports through ownershipAdapters.flint for receipt identity, then add this focused test to the Node manifest.
Regenerate packages/flint-wasm/release/production-kernel-coverage.json and Wasm capability/release receipts, rebuild the production artifact, and run the full native plus browser differential suites.
Declare and test fq_context, fq_element, and fq_polynomial for Wasm in a separate extension-algebra lane; do not reclassify those seven functions until actual lifecycle execution passes.
